title: Robison's rehearsals and business troubles
summary: Robison had fine studio musicians but was a poor businessman who lost his home.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And the other day I spent an awful lot of time trying to remember them. But they came so fast, and I would go up there with Willard and do this work with him. And, you know, his rehearsals were always nice. He had good studio musicians, bass clarinets, mostly clarinets, (inaudible) mostly saxophone and strings and viola. He had some fine musicians in there and some nice rehearsals and some nice sounds.

But Willard wasn't much of a businessman. He eventually lost his home. We started off one fall with the Maxwell House broadcast, and they catered to him. You know, they liked his music, and they wanted to do a lot. That's when we did a lot of this less work. I was quite busy, I remember.

Oh, this was -- this had to be around the early '30s, after I'd gotten out of the Whiteman band. When I was working with Shilkret Shooret -- I was doing a lot of freelancing then. And if these guys would go off the air, you had a lot of free time, and sometimes they'd go off -- and Willard would work during the summer.
